utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the witness is called, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What about calling the case, or would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I beg your pardon, Your Honour. Too enthusiastic. I'll curb my enthusiasm immediately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, you had something.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm trying to restrain myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, the way the matter was left yesterday in relation to Rule 73 was -- Your Honour very kindly indicated that we would have the opportunity of renewing our application, given the circumstances in which it had to be indicated yesterday. Your Honour, we do wish to do that. Rule 73, under the heading of "other motions," which is what we looked at relatively briefly yesterday, the procedure is that we are to make, if we wish to appeal the matter in relation to Mr. Deronjic we are to make a request for certification to be filed within seven days of the filing of the impugned decision. In a sense, it's all going slightly backwards at the moment, because Your Honours haven't yet had the opportunity of giving the full reasons you gave us a summary of the reasons, but clearly we can't wait to go through the formal steps and wait for the reasons and then file our request, because the whole thing will have moved on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be given full priority to give you the reasons, but you'll understand that even the Chamber now and then needs some time to write matters down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I don't wish it to be thought that there was the slightest implication of any complaint about the time being taken. It's just a question of where it leaves us procedurally in the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, procedurally, I would say the decision is there. You could already file a request and give your provisional reasons for that, and it goes without saying that you'll be allowed to complete the reasons for your request once you've received the written decision. Perhaps that's -- if you'd rather start right away, you could file a motion, file a request, and then give supplementary reasons once you've seen our written decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, in fact, what we have done, and this is subject to one of those slightly irritating matters which is simply the need to obtain sufficient photocopies. But what we have, in fact, got exactly that written application ready for by way of the request for certification, and I think one of the court officers is very kindly arranging sufficient photocopies even as we speak. As far as the proposal Your Honour has just made for filing supplementary reasons are concerned, the difficulty with this being that while it's part of our submissions in this document that we're about to file that the evidence given by Mr. Deronjic yesterday, although of course he began to go into some important issues, his evidence is not yet got so far that we reach a more or less irreversible position so far as his giving evidence is concerned. After all, the nature of our application, the nature of our appeal, would be that his evidence should be deferred. And that appeal really is rendered pretty useless if, while it's pending and while we're awaiting the reasons and while we're filing supplementary reasons, Mr. Deronjic is simply continuing with his evidence, because we will have a situation that he's given days and days of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we were aware of that when we yesterday took our decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I understand that, Your Honour, but it still leaves the question of an appeal, and it still leaves the issue which I believe that both Your Honours and we acknowledged yesterday had not presented the opportunity for anything approaching mature consideration, which was the way in which the conditions of 73(B) were intended to operate. And we have -- in the time available, we have had a look at the Tribunal case-law to see whether there is any helpful guidance in relation to that, and so far as -- you can never prove an absolute negative, but so far as we've been able to ascertain, there isn't anything which casts any particularly helpful guidance on that. So it becomes a matter of looking at that particular provision to see what it's intended to do. Your Honour, what I was going to propose, of course in the Tribunal's hands, was that we should in the circumstances, we should very briefly highlight our submissions this morning on this matter, because, after all, if the matter isn't dealt with, then what we would have to propose is that we request certification. If Your Honours give certification, then of course we are in a position to proceed with our appeal. We would, of course, be seeking that the Appeals Chamber would deal with the matter by way of expedition, which we expect they would be willing within the confines of what they can humanly do, they would naturally be willing to do, given the particular issue, and of course, the Appeals Chamber is then in control of precisely what procedures it adopts and what timetable it adopts to resolve the matter. But what would be important in the circumstances would be that Mr. Deronjic's evidence should be halted, because if we do proceed with his evidence -- well, I've already said that, Your Honour. It becomes impossible to untangle, in practice, if he continues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said it already yesterday even.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has decided that we'll continue to hear the evidence of Mr. Deronjic at this moment, and you can be assured that whatever is filed will be checked by us and we'll rethink during every break what to do. But we'll continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And Your Honours -- will Your Honours give the Defence an opportunity of developing submissions on this matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first see what you have written down on paper. We'll review that during the next break, to start with, and we'll also then decide whether there will be a moment for additional oral submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. I'm much obliged, Your Honour. In that case, Your Honour, since I can't do much with it over the next hour or so, this is the only copy I've got at the moment, but perhaps I can hand that up, on, if possible, the understanding that somebody will give me a copy back at some point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And even if it's not formally filed yet, courtesy copies will be read by the Judges anyhow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure precisely what the procedure is for filing, Your Honour, but as we have actually handed it to the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think a filing should be done at the registry downstairs because there it's all registered, et cetera, et cetera, which could -- but don't worry about that. This Chamber is not that formalistic that if we know that a document will be filed, and of course in full confidence that the filing will not be anything different from what we receive, we'll look at the courtesy copies already prior to filing, if urgency ask us to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. If my co-counsel won't sign it, well, it'll just go in signed by me. Your Honour, may I say: We undertake to file that at the first moment that one of our team can escape from Court, which would be the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Once the witness and counsel are in, the usher will immediately start making copies. But her first duty is to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Of course. We understand, Your Honour. We've obliged the help given this morning with this administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Usher, I think it's not yourself, but with the assistance of the security, could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Cvijetic in. Good morning, Mr. Deronjic. May I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've made yesterday. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, I would like to focus your attention on some additional aspects of how the SDS party organised itself in the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if I could have the next exhibit, please. Could I have its number, and if it could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P38.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If a copy of that could be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, have you seen this exhibit before you came into Court today?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon, I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this is a document that is dated the 15th of August, 1991. It comes from the president of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it is addressed to all municipal main board -- all municipal boards of the SDS in Bosnia and Herzegovina. And I would like your comments on this document, please. Could you tell the Judges, one, whether you have ever received a document similar to this; and could you tell the Judges what this document signifies.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. As president of the municipal board of the Serbian Democratic Party in Bratunac, I received this document in brief. It talks about certain disciplinary measures within the SDS. And in 1991, we received quite a lot of material of similar contents, where the SDS officials at the local level are instructed to a certain kind of behaviour in accordance with the directives of the Serbian Democratic Party. Actually, we could say that a kind of discipline was being introduced into the work of the local bodies of the SDS, and these guidelines for conduct are actually what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were these guidelines mandatory?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. The guidelines were binding, and we were obliged to respect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, on the B/C/S version that is before you, there appears at the bottom to be a stamp. Can you tell us what stamp that is?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the stamp of the Serbian Democratic Party, the stamp of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's a stamp used by the -- or signifying the Main Board. That is the only party stamp that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Deronjic. I'd like to turn your attention to an event that took place in the joint assembly on the 14th and 15th of October, 1991, where the deputies -- some of the deputies who were present passed a memorandum supporting the creation of a sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina. Can you tell us, first of all: Are you aware of that decision, that event?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't remember the month. The 14th and the 15th --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Of October 1991. Are you aware of what happened in the assembly on that date?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. This is what I understood. This is supposed to refer to 1991, at a session of the Joint Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The representatives of two peoples, Muslims and Croats, in the Joint Assembly supported the declaration on the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and practically from that date on, Bosnia and Herzegovina became an independent state, in accordance with the desire of those deputies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, there will be significant testimony about that particular event, but in terms of the SDS party, what did that event signify for the SDS party, in broad terms?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that event by an activity of the SDS which followed immediately after this assembly session. I will tell you what the first measure of the SDS was that I recall. We were invited on the 18th of October to an extraordinary meeting, an urgent meeting of the SDS Main Board. It was also attended by the presidents of the municipal boards. At this meeting, which was chaired by the presidency of the SDS, headed by Mr. Karadzic, we were given guidelines for conduct following this event, and the way we interpreted the event was the unconstitutional declaration of independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The guidelines were as follows: Public discussions were supposed to be held as soon as possible, to inform the people about the political importance of that event; and then according to these guidelines that we received, we were to urgently form crisis staffs of the Serbian people - that's what they were called - in the municipalities. We were also told then that the leadership of the party had decide that in the coming period - I think that the date was already set then - a referendum would be held for the opinion of the Serbian people to be heard on this event, and I think this referendum was held in November, with one question: Were the Serbian people in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia? I don't remember the exact wording of this question. Our task was to adhere to these measures for the conduct of the members of the SDS and to make preparations for the referendum. I remember that event. I think at the time it was also indicated. It was actually stated that we would form an assembly, a Serb assembly, comprising members of the Serbian ethnic group who were in the joint Bosnia and Herzegovina assembly, which actually did happen subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, at this particular meeting, you said that there were presidents from the SDS municipal boards. How many of the presidents from the SDS municipal boards do you recall attending that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all obliged to attend, and I cannot remember specifically that meeting, but I think practically all of them were present. There were many of us at this meeting, because this was a major political event.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And was this also a meeting that was a meeting with the Main Board as well?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, the Main Board, augmented by the presidents of the municipal boards, as well as by the party officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you said that you were given tasks to adhere to, and my question is: Were you given these tasks in the form of written documents and instructions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, and I've refreshed my memory from the minutes, I think that we received written documents about conduct. I think they were called guidelines for the conduct of the Serbian people or the SDS, in given circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And were you, as a municipal SDS president, duty-bound to adhere to those directives?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how I understood it from that meeting, that I was duty-bound to apply those guidelines. And then on the 19th, in Bratunac, I convened a session of the municipal board, at which these guidelines were discussed, and tasks were assigned for their implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In terms of the direction of the SDS party policy, did this meeting mark a significant event in your mind?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I think that that was a meeting which reflected the policy trends of the SDS in 1991. I think it was one of the most important meetings in relation to these new policies or this direction in the conduct of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was that direction the SDS was taking?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said very briefly yesterday - perhaps I went into too much detail - that in 1991 the direction of the SDS was to create Republika Srpska. This is one of the dates, or this meeting is one of the meetings which, in continuity, signifies a key event. Of course, the next one which marked the forming of the Serbian Assembly was also a major date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, having received these instructions, did you return to the Bratunac municipality and implement them? And you can answer that question yes or no at this point.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, my next exhibit is a photocopy of two volumes that I have received. Excuse me just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There apparently is a technical problem, Your Honours, but I think we can proceed. If it becomes a problem to Your Honours, I would ask the Court's indulgence for a brief recess while the technical problem can be cured. But I think we can proceed without resolving it at this point. Your Honour, what I'm going to -- my next exhibit is an exhibit that is in B/C/S. It has -- it's multiple pages and it is an identical copy of two originals volumes that I have taken out of the Evidence Unit. I have shown these to counsel. I'm prepared to let Your Honours inspect these. But the witness has asked that these originals be brought in because it's easier for him to answer questions by flipping through the pages in these documents. And my request of the Court is that I be permitted to have the witness have these two documents in front of him while I ask him questions. The exact materials are photocopied in the exhibit, and I have extracts that I will be referring to, and I will be submitting as exhibits. They will be both in the B/C/S language and in the English language.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we just be clear where this material is to be found? Mr. Harmon did of course kindly show the items to me for a brief inspection. I just wish to be clear at the moment. When he says that the exact materials are photocopied in the exhibit, I'm not quite sure physically what we're talking at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm talking about an exhibit that we have provided to you that is -- it has a logo on the front. You should have this. This was ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I understand -- I'm sorry. We don't have it in physical hard copy. So presumably it's on a CD. Could it just be indicated where it is? That's all I'm asking, actually, just a simple question. Through the Tribunal, if I may simply ask that. Because we're just trying to follow what's happening. Sort of part of our job.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm informed it was provided in CD.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's -- Your Honour, that's helpful only up to a point. Reference numbers are really very, very helpful. We do have quite a few dozens and hundreds of CDs. Well, hundreds is may be an exaggeration. I withdraw that. Certainly dozens. It feels like hundreds.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm informed, Your Honour, that the Defence received last night a list identifying this document, with an ERN number. This document also is part of an expert report that was filed - I don't know when - a year and a half ago. So this document has been available to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you: You say the Defence received the list last night. Was this document on any previous list, indicated as ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm informed that the Defence received a hard copy of this document on July 31st, 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question was whether it was listed on one of the previous lists. I mean, we have the very -- I would say the very practical problem that you can't review all CDs every night, so therefore, one of the reasons of the existence of these lists is that, at least well in advance, the attention is -- the attention is drawn to the fact that these exhibits will be presented at this stage of the proceedings. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the day before yesterday, a list was given to the Defence, listing this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Last night, another list was given to the Defence listing the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This document was part of -- a hard copy of this document was given, as I said, in July of 2002 to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it's -- I do understand it was in your view not only in the CD-ROM. Yes, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid that maybe there's some confusion. At the moment, we do not think that this list was given to us the day before yesterday. If Mr. Harmon is talking about some other list, well, that may be -- it may be true. Your Honour, can I say: The practical position, and Your Honour, after all, has some experience of sitting in a sense where I'm sitting, in relation to other matters. Documents supplied in July 2002, now, everybody knows that none of the current Defence -- well, Ms. Cmeric was involved but the present counsel were not involved at all. The real world is that we cannot trawl through boxes and boxes of documents picking out every document in B/C/S and bring it to Court with us in case it should be a document which will be referred to in a particular week on a particular day. That's simply human not possible. Similarly, when we are provided with CD material, with sometimes limited clues as to where it's going and what's on it, and labels which are simply numbers that we can't cross-check, Your Honour knows that, as you've said, we can't just in an evening go through a CD and identify everything. So far as this list -- may I just add, Your Honour, third point, with respect: We did discuss with Mr. Harmon yesterday the absence in relation to this witness as he began his evidence of the type of list of exhibits which we have been given in relation to previous witnesses, and I understood that the Prosecution had had their own problems, because everybody has their own problems, in producing that list. But we have all been handicapped by the absence of that list. So the point of my question just now really was just to know where this stuff is. I can now see it. I now see it. I have the CD -- well, in fact I've got it copied onto a hard disk. I have it on my computer. While we've been talking over the last few minutes, I see it, I have it up on my computer. But realistically and humanly, it's not a task that we were able to do from being provided with a CD with all the exhibits yesterday evening. All I'm asking for, sometimes, is, in the difficult circumstances that we all face, just a little bit more practical help and guidance as to where material can be found. Because to say, well, you've had it, it's there somewhere, you've got it, you were given it in 2002 or it's on a CD is not going to enable the Defence to do its job and it's not going to enable this trial to proceed properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may respond briefly. I want the record to be clear on this. We didn't tell the Defence it's on a CD, go look for it. Two days ago we gave the Defence a list identifying the document, identifying the ERN number, both in the B/C/S version and in the English version. Last night we reordered the exhibit list, and we gave them a second list identifying the same materials in the same form. So this is not a situation of trying to find a needle in a haystack. This is a situation where two days ago they were directed specifically to this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if we might, to clarify this, may we be simply shown this list that we said -- I don't say we weren't, but at the moment I'm simply mystified. If I could have a look at this list that apparently we were given two days ago, then I would know what we're talking about. But I am handicapped at the moment, Your Honour. Maybe it's my fault. I hope I shall graciously withdraw if it turns out we've had something which made it all crystal clear and we overlooked it, but at the moment I simply don't know what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see. I do understand that on this list -- and the Chamber has received copies of this list, The first one without the trial exhibit numbers on it yet and the second one with for the first five, or I should say, seven documents the numbers P33 until P37. Where does it appear exactly on the list, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have a list, Your Honour. It is on page 2 of the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The first list.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I apologise. It is page 2 of the list, third and the fourth item down on that list. It says: "Minutes of assembly sessions," and it says number of pages to the right, 91 and 97.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That appears quite, I would say, not on top of the list, but it's among the first ten items. I think that was on the original list. I think at this very moment the most important thing is whether the -- first of all, whether the Defence would have a hard copy or could be provided with a hard copy so that it would be more easy to follow the testimony to be given by this witness. Would there be any other suggestion to stop on this point or ...? Mr. Stewart, you have explained your difficulties and you've said what you would like to have done in a different way, but now let's be practical and see what consequences this should result in at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting -- we're not -- we're not, I think, right now handicapped in any way that there's any reason for the evidence not to proceed, but can I just say, Your Honour: I'm still not sure that we have a list dated 12/02/04, 1802. That's what we're looking at this morning. Now, if a moment ago Your Honour or Mr. Harmon were looking at a different list, just within the last two or three minutes when he was referring to this item, then I'm back to the point I made: I don't know what list it is we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've got two lists in front of me. The first one, the 12th of the second -- of 2004, time 8:41. The other one is the 12th of the 2nd, 04, 18 hours, 20 minutes. We find that in the bottom of the -- of all pages, right-hand bottom. But the documents appear on both lists, and the easiest way is to find the number of pages, and on the -- well, let's say the early list, it appears on page 2, items 3 and 4, and on the other list. I must say, the time indicated only appears on the -- there's a cover sheet, I see, and a time and a date appears only on the next pages, which start with 1. So the structure of the pages is on from page 2 of that last document the same, but it in addition has a cover sheet where we mainly find the numbers P33 and up until P37. Perhaps I just show to you, this is the cover page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May I just comment. The two lists Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Now I turned my microphone on. The two lists that Your Honour is referring to are both dated the 12th of February, which is yesterday. The timing of the later one is slightly different, perhaps it's just a different printout, because our timing is 1802. But may I observe that the earlier one that Your Honour referred to was dated, timed 8:41 yesterday morning. Well, at 8:41 yesterday morning the Defence team is really involved in that very important technical tasks of making sure our wigs are straight and we're ready to come into Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's be practical. Whatever has to be clarified, in view of lists and whether they are given are not, is not something we should go through in detail at this very moment. I did understand that for the continuation of the examination-in-chief at this moment, there are no insurmountable problems. Let's proceed with that. Let's see if there's any matter to be clarified, let the parties see whether they could do that during the break, and if there's any remaining issue we'll hear from you. Mr. Harmon, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, may I then have first of all these exhibits passed to Your Honours if Your Honours wish to inspect them, and then to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can I ask the registrar for the exhibit number of the copy that we will be tendering into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For ERN number 02192709, it will be Prosecution Exhibit number P39. And for document bearing ERN number 02192549, it will be Prosecution Exhibit number P40.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, in front of you are two volumes. Before we go into those volumes, I would like to ask you some questions about them. Can you identify those volumes? Can you tell the Judges what they are, when they were prepared, and how they were prepared. And if you wait just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. These are records, or minutes, from all the sessions of the municipal board of the SDS, from 1990 to spring 1996, that is, all sessions of the municipal board that I held in Bratunac, for which the minutes were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you recognise those documents as being the proper minutes?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are original minutes, bearing all the signatures of the recording secretary and my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me return to your testimony relating to the meeting in Sarajevo on the 18th of October, 1991. You said that you returned to Bratunac, understanding instructions that you had received, and you implemented those in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have the next exhibit shown to the witness, which is an extract from these minutes. For the help of the registrar, these start out with minutes, and then it says "of the emergency meeting."

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P41.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Harmon. I'm ready --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Just wait a minute, Mr. Deronjic. We seem to have another technical problem. Perhaps, rather than delay while we try to resolve the technical problem: The registrar has a copy of the English version that can be put on the screen - on the ELMO, I'm sorry - and we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, do you have before you the minutes of the meeting that were convened upon your return to Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And are these the minutes that are in the exhibit that are before you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you explain what you did when you returned to Bratunac after that meeting on the 18th of October.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon return from the session of the Main Board, held in Sarajevo on the 18th October, 1991, as written in these minutes, I informed the municipal board on the stances taken by the Main Board and the measures that were adopted as guidelines for the conduct of local organs. From these minutes, we can see that we indeed applied all these measures. We appointed a commission for carrying out of a plebiscite of the Serbian people, elected five members on to this commission, elected also a Crisis Staff of the Serbian People, of which I became the president. We furthermore agreed on guard duty in party offices and scheduled a public debate in Bratunac to acquaint the citizenship with the guidelines that were ordered by the Main Board to be implemented in municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if you could turn, Mr. Deronjic, to point 5. And please, if that could be shown on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- the Chamber would like to see not only the upper part of the first page, but just briefly also the down parts. If we could go back to page 1, and also have just a glance on the -- yes. Yes. We could now move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if we can start at the top of the page and do the same thing for the Judges and then end on paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm reading slowly, but not that slowly. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, I invite your comments on paragraph 5, please. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac, Mr. Rodoljub Djukanovic, as far as I can remember, informed the municipal board of the SDS about the process of regionalisation, that is, activities related to the creation of Serbian Autonomous districts. There is somewhere in the minutes one meeting where we accepted the initiative to create the Serbian Autonomous District of Birac, which included the municipality of Bratunac, and then at the following meeting we adopted a decision to support the establishment of the Birac Autonomous District, which was established in January. The last one out of all these regional communities to be formed. And then the current conclusion is to acquaint the population as soon as possible with the new situation, in keeping with the decision of the Main Board to hold public debates and to acquaint the citizenship with the current situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Deronjic. We'll move to the next exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Can I just clarify, Your Honour? That seems to us, unless I'm mistaken, that seems to be pages 84 and 85. It's listed as page 83 on the printout, but I -- it's coming up as pages 84 and 85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that a matter of translation? Is the original 83? Perhaps the witness could check in the original whether what he finds on --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The page reference is given under the translation column, Your Honour, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen that. It says 83. But we could perhaps check in the original. Yes. Could you please open the original, perhaps put it on the ELMO, and show us page 83. And if you do not find anything there, page 84 and 85.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It could be a translation error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It may be a reference to the translation page number. That's what I'm thinking.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand that. I'm looking at the translation and it's pages 84 and 85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it's a reference to the original. That's what I'm trying to check. Could we put the original page 83 on the ELMO. Could I just have the original. The problem seems to be, Mr. Harmon, that there is no original page numbering in the handwritten copies, so the pages must refer to anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I believe those might be -- the translators have put in those numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you try to find out that. We know at this moment what translation we have, and during the break we -- I take it there is nothing in the translation which does not appear in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's what I'm informed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it says 83 of 86, and since the number of pages is 91 and 97, the first, P41.1, translation ERN says page 33. On the bottom of the page I find 83 of 86, and then on the second page, I find 84 of 86. So I take it that the correct indication for P41 in translation would be pages 83 and 84 out of 86, of the translation numbering. But, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, can I just -- it isn't -- it isn't that I'm trying to be difficult. Some may say I don't need to try, that it comes naturally. But the position, Your Honour, is this: That, for example, I am working now, as I take it I've been invited to do, I'm working from the CD of exhibits -- well, in fact I've copied the contents over to a hard disk but for practical purposes I'm working from a CD of exhibits that I've been provided with, and on that, the numbering is, as I've indicated to Your Honour, it's pages 84 and 85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So it's only this, Your Honour, if I may say. This is only one tiny point and I acknowledge the Prosecution have their difficulties; nobody can get everything right all the time. It only this seems a tiny point but when it's multiplied Your Honour knows that every time we come across this sort of difficulty, that can be another five or ten minutes sorting it out when we're trying to prepare work on the case. That's all. And these are cumulative difficulties when we're under enormous pressure anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's my experience that sometimes by copying documents, page numbering, especially if this is automatic page numbering, sometimes differs as well. I'm aware of the problem. Let's concentrate at this moment on the content, and whenever it would bother you in such a way that you have difficulties in following the testimony, then of course we will deal with it during the hearing. If it's a problem that could be solved during a break or if can could be clarified during a break, the Chamber would appreciate if the parties would try to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Deronjic, we have finished with P41. I'd like to go to the next exhibit, please. And I assume that will be P42.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P42.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if those -- the English version of that could be placed on the ELMO, and the B/C/S version given to Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We'll start with just showing on the ELMO the top of this -- Mr. Deronjic, take a moment and examine, please, the B/C/S version of Exhibit P42. Mr. Deronjic, does this appear to be the minutes from an SDS municipal board session held on the 25th of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the minutes from that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And was this meeting in respect of continuing to implement the directives that you had received on the 18th of October in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. As far as I can understand now, this meeting took place a few days after this first meeting, and then the election of the Crisis Staff was confirmed at the meeting, and then further details about the plebiscite were developed a little more. A commission was also elected for propaganda and technical assistance in the implementation of the plebiscite. Also, the agenda was augmented with a decision on regionalisation. So in item 4, it says that the assembly accepts the decision -- the board on the formation of the Autonomous Region of Birac, and therefore we accepted the idea of regionalisation, which resulted in the creation of the Birac region in January of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And could you comment on item number 1 on the agenda. I'm sorry. Item number 1 below the five items listed on the agenda. Starting -- I'll read it for you to orient you. "The president briefly introduced the board with the founding of the Serbian Assembly, its tasks and aims. The board unanimously accepted all the tasks." Can you comment on that, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were told on the 18th of October that a Serbian assembly would be formed, and what its tasks would be, and they were preparations to establish Republika Srpska. I informed the board about this briefly, as much as I was able to do, based on the information from that meeting. The board unanimously accepted these tasks that we were supposed to implement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Deronjic. Now, we have talked about the 18th of October, 1991 meeting. I would now like to fast-forward two months to a meeting that was held in Sarajevo on the 19th of December, 1991. And I'd ask you if you can tell us about the meeting that took place on that date. First of all, if you could tell us who summoned you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting of the 19th -- I'm not sure about the dates. I said that during the interview. The meeting was held on or about the 19th of December, in Sarajevo, in 1991. I went there at the invitation of the party secretariat. I cannot remember exactly who invited me. The meeting was of a similar kind. It was an expanded meeting of the Main Board, including party officials and the presidents of the municipal boards. I remember the date also, because during those few days - I don't know exactly whether it was the 20th or the 21st - an assembly session was held, at which the assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina was established. At this meeting, which took place one day before or one day after this assembly session - I really don't remember - received documents about the future conduct of the party officials and the Serbian people in general. I think that's what it was called. And this document -- or the measures are known as Variant A and B, and these measures were supposed to be implemented in the field by all the party organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, Mr. Deronjic, to identify, if you can, the people you remember who were present at that meeting. You've identified the fact that there were SDS municipal board presidents, expanded Main Board. Can you just fill in by identifying by name the people you saw at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an assembly session that was a key event during those days, the convening of the Serbian Assembly. At that meeting, I saw, as far as I can remember, the top officials of the Serbian Democratic Party, including the party presidency, including Mr. Krajisnik, who was preparing the assembly session. The meeting about the A and B variant materials was held independently of the assembly session, of course, and the only thing that I remember from that meeting -- of course, all the members of the Main Board were present, and officials of the party, local ones too. I couldn't really remember the individual -- every individual who attended it at the time, but I know that that meeting, where the A and B variant materials were presented, was chaired by Mr. Karadzic. I remembered some of his sentences and some of the views he expressed regarding the self-organising of Serbs out in the field. To make it brief: It was a well-known event, attended by all the top party officials and people who had to date participated in the joint authorities: Mr. Koljevic, Mrs. Plavsic. I'm not sure whether I saw you all of them, but I did see some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see Goran Zekic from a neighbouring municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We travelled together. Goran Zekic and myself. We most often went to all of those meetings together. Zekic was also a member of the assembly. He was a deputy in the assembly, so he was obliged to attend the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see Brano Grujic, from the Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned the names of the people. I tried to recall them. I'm not sure whether I saw him or not. I more or less mentioned the people who should have been there. I think I did see him there, but I cannot be 100 per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And what about Rajko Dukic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Dukic did attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if I can have the next exhibit, please. And I am informed that there is no technical problem at the moment, so it will appear on the screen. Thank you to the registrar for assisting me with the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number P43.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, let me ask you if you have seen a copy of this document before coming in to testify.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We received this document in 1991, at this meeting that I discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this is -- the document that is in front of you is a copy, copy number 100. You mentioned that you received a copy of a document before you left. Did the other presidents of the municipal boards also receive copies of the same document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know if this was the copy that was provided to you or was provided to somebody else? Are you able to tell?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. What do you mean, "this copy?" Do you mean the contents of this copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The contents of this copy.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I am trying to go through the whole thing to the end. I think that that is the content. I cannot read everything right now, but I believe, yes, that that is the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May I have the assistance of the usher one more time, please. If I could have the English translation. This is a mistranslation, the copy that is on the computer screen. I apologise to the Court. If I could have the English version placed on the ELMO. Actually, now the proper translation has appeared on the screen, so I'm getting used to this technology, Your Honour. I apologise. I don't need this placed on the ELMO any longer. The proper translation has been placed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, if you look at the upper left-hand corner of the document before you, can you tell us who issued these instructions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instructions were issued by the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in the upper right-hand corner, it says: "Strictly confidential."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The material was strictly confidential. That's what it said on the material itself. And I must say that we also in the municipalities applied a certain degree of confidentiality, perhaps not a strict confidentiality as it is stated here, but we did have such materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, who instructed you at that meeting about the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic gave us the instructions on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were comments on events that had taken place before in the light of that event, in particular, of the 14th and the 15th of October, when it was noted that -- and of course I'm not quoting; I'm just trying to remember the sense of it, the sense of the address by Mr. Karadzic, and that that event, the voting and the support of the declaration for the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina was an unconstitutional act and that it represented a violation of the basic rights of the Serbian people as a constitutive people of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that these measures, these confidential members which we received on the organising, as we called them, on the self-protection of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that these measures we were duty-bound to implement in the municipalities. They represented a form. Besides the measures which we were to implement, they were a kind of extraordinary circumstance within the SDS, and you can see from the material that it was necessary to convene daily meetings of crisis staffs, municipal boards, and so on. And I remembered that meeting. I'm only able to quote one sentence spoken by Mr. President, that we were duty-bound to ensure contacts with every man - they were thinking of Serbs - in the municipality and, if possible, if there were no other contacts, we were obliged to ensure physical contacts with people in the field, by messenger or courier. That's what it was said. And it was suggested that municipal boards should distribute amongst the officials in the local boards the number of families that they would be in charge of. We're not only talking about discipline, but a kind of care for these people; to monitor their health situation, their social situation, and, amongst other things, absolute discipline, and that people should be connected amongst themselves out in the field, meaning that the officials of the SDS were supposed to create a network which would cover all the people. That was the gist of Mr. Karadzic's address.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did these instructions make a distinction between municipalities where Serbs were in the majority of the population and where they were in the minority of the population?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was obliged to implement these documents, and I had a clear concept of what they were. There was Variant A and Variant B. The Variant A referred to municipalities in which the Serbs were in a majority, and it wasn't something that was interesting for the Bratunac municipality. Variant B represented a programme of measures for those municipalities which had a minority Serb population. Both the variants had two levels. There were two levels or degrees of mobility, or mobilisation, out in the field. The first level, which I would qualify as a milder level, which was introduced right away at that meeting itself, the introduction or application of level 1 was declared right there. Level 2 was something that depended on the circumstances and that we would be informed later when that would be applied. So the variants A and B represented the options for those municipalities which had either a majority or a minority Serb population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, you moved to the next subject, but one thing is not clear to me from the previous subject. You said it was not all about discipline, but it was also about discipline. Discipline to do what? To send your children in time to school, or what was this "discipline" about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, they talked about discipline in the party organs, and a kind of mobility of the party organs, as well as a discipline implementation of the tasks which the municipal board would assign to the local boards within a municipality. That was the kind of discipline they meant. Secondly, there were instructions that already for stage 1, you had to have regular daily meetings of the municipal and regional boards, and then we had to report back on these meetings to the Main Board and the presidency of the party at the republican level. That is the kind of discipline that they meant. It constituted a kind of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you are raising the issue of discipline not in relation to party discipline but in the context of responsibility to keep close contact with, I think it was 10 or 20 families. My question is: Were these families also expected to behave in a disciplinary way, and was that the reason that people would even seek physical contact with these families?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I understood, these were security measures, Your Honour, in the sense of informing people about certain extraordinary circumstances. So the local boards were entrusted with staying in contact with the local population in case of certain measures. Let's say in case of some kind of alert or the outbreak of hostilities. So in cases like that, the local boards would be able to convey to the population what had happened and to also provide some kind of care for those people in such an event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We were talking about discipline, not about taking care of what could happen to those families. But we're talking about discipline in relation to these families. What kind of discipline were they expected to show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The population, Your Honour, at that time - perhaps I misspoke - no discipline was expected of them. But the officials of the SDS were expected to take care about their own conduct, to make sure that their conduct was disciplined at that point. We even adopted a measure forbidding the officials from leaving, the SDS officials from being absent during such periods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then read to you what your testimony was in this respect. You said that: "It was suggested that the municipal boards should distribute amongst the official and the local boards the number of families that they would be in charge of. We're not only talking about discipline, but a kind of care for these people, to monitor their health situation, their social situation, and, amongst other things, absolute discipline." I take it that taking care of the health situation and taking care of the social situation was directly related in your answer to the families, and in your answer I see not any distinction that the discipline was for the party officials and that the health care was for the families. So my direct question to you is: Were the families expected to join in discipline together with the party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Such conduct was expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is a bit contrary to what you said one minute ago. But discipline in respect of what exactly? Not intervening if any armed activity would come up, in leaving the villages, if ordered? What kind of discipline were they expected to show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we skipped a topic, or some activities which we implemented in the course of the summer, and that was the arming of the people. A large number of the population at the time, on one side and the other, were armed. In Bratunac, there were a number of conflicts already in the previous period. The disciplinary measures obliged people to behave in accordance with the instructions of the organs of the SDS in the field, so with the instructions of the local boards who were in charge of that region. What these could be depends on the events that could ensue, but they were duty-bound to carry out the measures of the local board in a disciplined way, which they would be instructed to do. Sometimes there was guard duty that was required, or, for example, the securing of some key facilities, or the possibility for the preparation of food reserves in that area. This is what I was thinking of, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your answer, you also spoke about the population being armed on both sides. Would the discipline also cover the receiving arms and keeping arms available for events to come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would the discipline be also expected from Serbs who were not party members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were different views on this, but I think that it -- the population was supporting the SDS, and this was expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was not asking whether they were supporting the SDS, but whether this discipline was also expected from non-party members. And you say it was expected from them, at least if I understand your testimony correctly, it was expected from them, but it caused no problems because they were in support of the party anyhow, even if not members. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Perhaps we didn't understand one another very well. When we were forming the Crisis Staff in the municipality, according to instructions from October 1991, the Crisis Staff was called the Crisis Staff of the Serbian People, with the obvious intent that it should encompass the entire Serb population, regardless of party affiliation. And we were instructed to hold public panel discussions and to inform the people about the measures that we were implementing, and to see whether the people were supporting what we were doing. I did hold such a discussion panel. I did inform the people at a public gathering about these measures, and I did receive support. Nobody was opposed to my stance. The Crisis Staff of the Serbian People which we formed also included non-party people. There are their names here in the minutes, and I can tell you exactly which prominent figures were included in this category.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not asking you that. I'm just drawing your attention to when you talked about discipline, it was about SDS, and now we hear that there was some relevant information as far as crisis staffs are concerned as well. I intervened. I have no further questions. But at the same time, it's 10.30, so I'd like to have a break, and we'll adjourn until 5 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Before I continue with my examination, Your Honour, I wish to inform the Court that during the discussion on when the lists were provided to Defence counsel, I had been informed that the first list was provided two days ago. During the recess -- I therefore informed the Court of that. I had been informed during the recess that indeed the list was provided to the Defence yesterday morning, the first list, and the second list at around 6.00. So I apologise for providing incorrect information to the Court, and I apologise to counsel as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, the apology is accepted, Your Honour, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, we were talking about Variant A and Variant B, the document that is marked "strictly confidential." Can you tell the Trial Chamber why this document was marked "strictly confidential"?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I think it's strictly confidential because I suppose it was not meant to fall into the hands of the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I suppose that's the reason. We were not specifically told why it was strictly confidential, or at least I don't remember that we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in your view, Mr. Deronjic, what was the purpose of organising in this fashion?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the Serbs organising themselves in this fashion was twofold, I believe. One was to implement measures to create Republika Srpska, because Variant B implies the establishment of parallel institutions at the municipal level. And when I say "parallel," I mean purely Serbian as opposed to the institutions that were in place at the time. Whereas in Variant B, it implied the association and linkage of Serbian municipalities into one entity. At that time, republican departments -- republican authorities were formed, such as police centres, parallel to the existing ones at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And on the other hand, these documents were meant to help the Serbian people organise themselves, in view of the war and possible threats and conflicts breaking out, because the implementation of this radical plan of creating Republika Srpska implied the possibility of war. I must remind you that all these events took place against the background of the open war raging in the Republic of Croatia, which was followed closely in our country.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have the next exhibit in order given an exhibit number and presented to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit number P44.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, upon receiving these confidential instructions, did you return to Bratunac with them and take steps to implement them?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. On the 23rd December 1991, four days after my return from Sarajevo, or wherever it was - whenever it was exactly that this meeting in Sarajevo took place - we held a meeting of the municipal board, and the agenda included review of the decision and documents of the meeting of the SDS in Sarajevo, and we adopted certain decisions related to the background material I brought from that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And is Prosecutor's Exhibit 44 the minutes from that meeting that was held on the 23rd of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I don't see this mark, P40 -- yes, I see it here on top. P44, yes. Those are the minutes of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in -- you've described this document as making a distinction between municipalities where Serbs are in the minority, Variant B. And in this case, the Bratunac municipality, as you said, was a Variant B municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And under these confidential instructions, you were to take certain steps, certain specified steps. Mr. Deronjic, did you take all of the steps that were required, or can you describe to the Court what steps you did take.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took most of the steps indicated in the documents that I had brought from the meeting of the Main Board of the SDS. These meetings largely reflect all the measures that we took. We scheduled a founding meeting of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bratunac and we adopted the decision to hold this assembly on the 12th of December, 1991. Just a minute. Let me check. Sorry. 30th December. And there are minutes of that assembly meeting. In other words, we formed a parallel assembly in Bratunac, involving all Serbian MPs and Serbs who were deputies representing the SDP party. Other parties were not represented in the assembly at all. Then we decided to form the Crisis Staff of the SDS. I want to clarify here that for practical reasons in Bratunac, we did not form a separate crisis staff, as the documents instructed us, because, according to the instruction of the 18th of October, a crisis staff had already been formed, and we just verified this existing crisis staff as the SDS Crisis Staff. Furthermore, we introduced guard duty in the municipal board of the SDS and in all the local boards, and we conveyed to the local boards all the measures to be taken regarding networking, linking all the people into one network and securing a smooth flow of information towards people in the field. All these steps were taken, and from that point on we started to engage in the activities of the crisis staff, which we formalised as the SDS Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now if I could have the next exhibit marked, please. If that exhibit could be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution exhibit number P45.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, take a moment to cast your eye on that. Mr. Deronjic, you described these confidential instructions as having two phases: Phase 1 and phase 2. Did you eventually receive instructions to implement phase 2 of Variant A and Variant B? You can answer that yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who ordered it implemented?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order came from the Main Board, and it was related to us by Mr. Zekic, Mr. Goran Zekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And Mr. Goran Zekic at the time was a member of the Main Board; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, having received that instruction from Mr. Zekic, did you indeed implement phase 2 of Variant A and B, and does Prosecutor's Exhibit 45 represent the minutes of a meeting held in the municipal board on the 24th of February, 1992, where those -- the second phase was implemented?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We introduced the second phase of the Variant A and Variant B documents, and this document represents the minutes of the meeting of the municipal board of the 24th February 1992. Just one thing: It says here "minutes of the meeting of the Main Board." It is no Main Board. It is the municipal board. It must be an error made by the recording secretary who erroneously typed "Main Board." It was the municipal board of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, could that be checked? Because in the English translation, it reads "municipal board," which of course could cause some doubt in the quality of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's what my exhibit reflects as well, and this is an official translation. So I will check and we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, could you please read the first line of these minutes and then slowly, please, so that we can get it translated, and we have to see whether there is really a question of a translation problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency. "Minutes of the meeting of the Main Board held on the 24th of February, 1992, starting at 1700 hours." And then it says: "35 deputies --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Perhaps it could be just corrected orally in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since we now have -- first of all, the witness has drawn our attention to it, secondly, it's confirmed by the translators. So therefore I'd rather not send the document back to the translation services and deal with it in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the first item on the agenda, according to these minutes, Mr. Deronjic, was the implementation of level 2, the state of emergency. My question to you is: Was that agenda item adopted unanimously?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't remember the meeting itself, but it says in the minutes that the agenda was adopted unanimously.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, what role and importance did phase 2 of Variant A and B instructions have in respect of the developments in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Can you comment on that, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second degree, or second phase, of variants A and B implied the introduction of new measures in the organising of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that primarily referred to the establishment of parallel institutions. According to variants A and B, it was our duty to establish the assembly, and in the second phase of Variant B, we were to form a complete executive board of the Serbian assembly at the local level. I must say that for various reasons we didn't do that in Bratunac, because we held this session of the assembly belatedly. Then Variant B also envisages the establishment of other parallel institutions, primarily police ones and security institutions, such as the Territorial Defence, the judiciary, health care institutions, separation of education establishments. All these were measures envisaged by Variants A and B in their second stage. And we adapted in Bratunac these measures, because we were not able to strictly follow these orders, for a number of reasons. And if you need clarification, I will be happy to provide it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you clarify that very briefly, Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't be very brief, but I'll try. We did not have the practical possibilities for forming parallel institutions, and that's why we gave up on that immediately. On the other hand, there were misgivings, and perhaps a not complete understanding of all this, and that's why we held a session of the municipal board, in its enlarged composition, to include representatives of the local boards, because we were afraid of conflicts arising, because Bratunac was already living in a very tense atmosphere. We decided to maintain contacts with Muslim representatives, to hold regular assembly sessions, joint assembly sessions, and to try at those joint sessions to agree on some acceptable measures envisaged by these Variants A and B, such as separating the police force in Bratunac. We managed to agree on that and we implemented that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that explanation, Mr. Deronjic. I'd like to change the topic and I'd like to focus on a new area, and that is the subject of how the Bosnian Serbs from your region received weapons. And I would like you, Mr. Deronjic, to focus your attention to sometime around approximately April of 1991, and ask you: When was the first time that you became aware that weapons were being provided to the Serbian people in your region?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first learned of this arming in an organised form in April 1991, at a meeting between Mr. Dukic, president of the Executive Board of SDS; Goran Zekic; and myself. That was held in Milici in the second half of April, towards the end of April perhaps. I can't remember the exact date, but I remember the venue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mr. Deronjic. Just stop, because we're still getting acquainted with many of these figures in the SDS. Can you inform the Judges -- you said Mr. Dukic. Is that Rajko Dukic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you inform the Judges a little bit about Mr. Dukic, who he is, what the positions he held in the SDS party, and what influence you believe he had in that party.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the SDS was established, I didn't know Mr. Dukic. I had only heard of him. He was a businessman, director, one of the largest companies in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the pre-war period, namely, the bauxite mine in Milici, which used to be part of a single municipality, Vlasenica. Mr. Dukic is one of the founders of the SDS. I must say that there was an opinion, for which I have no basis, namely, that he was one of the major financiers of the Serbian Democratic Party. I have no proof of that and I'm just relating this opinion. And Mr. Dukic was the first president of the Executive Board of the SDS. He enjoyed great authority in the SDS, and in 1991, in 1992, he was a prominent member. He later changed his views after the war, but that doesn't matter now. He was the highest political authority, the most prominent politician in the municipality of Birac, and he was thought and said to be a man who wielded great influence in the business circles of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, you just -- part of your answer was that there was an opinion about Mr. Dukic, one of the major financiers, and you added to that that was an opinion and you had no basis for it and no proof for it. That means that it's rumour. That is not of great assistance for the Chamber, unless you could tell us through which channels that rumour came to you, what would have been the source. I'm not saying that you couldn't tell us about anything for which you had not solid proof, but you added already here that, as a matter of fact, there was no basis whatsoever for yourself to assess even the credibility of these rumours, and that does not assist the Chamber. You were not specifically asked for it, but I'd like you to keep that in mind while giving your answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I see an error in the record as well, Your Honour. It says -- strike that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mr. Deronjic: At this meeting in April with Rajko Dukic, Goran Zekic, and yourself, in Milici, in April, can you tell us what was said and who said what?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that meeting, and I remember that Mr. Dukic passed on to us the information that it had been decided at a high level that Serbs in Bosnia should arm themselves. When he said "at a high level," he did not specify, but he added one sentence that I remember, namely, that Mr. Karadzic personally convinced Mr. Milosevic that Serbs in Bosnia should arm themselves. We discussed this, and to be completely precise, I remember most clearly the instructions he gave to Mr. Zekic and myself regarding distribution of arms. He said we were in charge of the municipalities we were representing, and he gave a paper to Mr. Zekic which, as I later learnt, contained the name and the telephone numbers of the man we were supposed to contact in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did Mr. Karadzic, in a conversation with you, later inform you about his role in the arming of the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This has nothing to do with a conversation in which I would have been informed. It is an utterance that I heard Mr. Karadzic made at one of the meetings, where he repeated that he personally had convinced Mr. Milosevic that Serbs should arm themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, after that meeting concluded in Milici, and Goran -- I'm sorry. Did you and Goran Zekic return to your respective municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did Mr. Zekic tell you who was in charge of the entire arming operation?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV DERONJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zekic told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
